# Known divergences: Layers

## Inline eval layers

A direct `eval` of a string literal (or of a text the layer folder computes from built-ins) is replaced by the code it runs when the code behaves the same in place. The rule, per site:

- `eval` is the global one: no binding named `eval` anywhere, no write to it, no enclosing `with`, no other sloppy direct `eval` whose text may declare `eval` in the site's function or one around it (that includes a peeled text that itself calls `eval`), and the program after the rewrite passes the built-in scan for `eval` and the folded built-ins (default lane: intact; `--unsafe`: intact or aliased).
- The text parses as a script under the strictness of the site and passes its early-error checks, every regular expression literal in it uses only the flags `gimsuy` (none twice) and passes the evaluator's own strict pattern grammar for those flags (which also refuses valid but less common syntax: lookarounds, named groups and back-references to them, `\c`, legacy octal and `\0`, `\u{...}`, property escapes, an empty class, a class escape in a range, characters outside the BMP and, under `u`, outside ASCII), has no `return`, `new.target`, `super`, `import()` or `import.meta`, and no label when the site is labelled; `await`/`yield` names are refused inside async functions and generators.
- A statement whose text declares nothing is spliced in place; one that declares only `let`/`const`/`class` is wrapped in a block. A text with `var` or function declarations is spliced only as a direct statement of a function body with simple parameters, when no other code in that function (closures included) names any declared name, the function has no other `eval` or `with`, and the names are not `arguments` or `eval`. In sloppy code the text must not `delete` a name or call `eval` (eval-declared bindings are deletable, inlined ones are not).
- A sloppy site whose text starts with `"use strict"` runs as `(() => { "use strict"; ... })()`, which keeps `this`, `arguments` and the text's own var scope. Where the site is the body of an `if`, a loop or a label, the call is wrapped in a block.
- A site inside a class field initialiser or static block, or inside an arrow function in one, is kept (there `arguments` in the text is an early error).
- An `eval` used as a value is replaced by `(0, <expression>)` when the text is one expression statement, so a function in it gets no inferred name and a member call loses its receiver as it did.
- `//# sourceURL=` and `//# sourceMappingURL=` comments in the text are dropped.

Divergences: the source text of a function that held the `eval` changes (`Function.prototype.toString`), error stacks no longer name the `sourceURL`, and the inlined code runs one frame shallower.

Premise: the text is judged by the grammar of the engine that runs the output. Syntax only some engines accept (optional chaining, private names, newer regular expression features) is inlined when it parses, so a feature test such as `try { eval("a?.b") } catch {}` loses its fallback branch on an engine without it. Regular expressions are the exception above.

## Function layers

`Function(params, body)(args)` is peeled to `(function anonymous(params) { body })(args)`. That function expression binds `anonymous` inside itself, which the function `Function` makes does not, so the layer is kept when the body names `anonymous` or contains a direct `eval` (which could read the name at run time).

Built-in scan (default lane) is an allowlist. A built-in root (`Object`, `Array`, `Function`, `Reflect`, `Symbol`, `String`, `Number`, `JSON`, `Math`, `Promise`, the other listed constructors and the fold's own roots), the global object (`globalThis`, `window`, `self`, `global`, script-level `this`) and a code runner (`eval`, `Function`, `execScript`, also read off the global object as `globalThis.eval`, and the timers and host schedulers `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `setImmediate`, `requestAnimationFrame` (and its prefixed forms), `requestIdleCallback`, `queueMicrotask` and `postTask`, which run a text or call back with the global object as `this` in browsers) may appear only as: a call or read of a listed static member (`Object.keys`, `Array.isArray`, `Math.max`, `Symbol.iterator`, ...), a read of a listed method on its `prototype` (used as a value or through `call`/`apply`/`bind`, never called with the prototype as receiver), `new Root(...)`, a direct call of a non-runner root, a direct call of a timer whose first argument is a function (a function expression or arrow, a name bound only to function declarations or function expressions and never written, or `.bind(...)` on one of these), `typeof`, a comparison or `instanceof`, a test, or a member of the global object that names no built-in. Any other appearance (a value, a logical/conditional/comma wrapper used as an object, `.constructor`, `["prototype"]`, `call`/`apply`/`bind` on a runner, an install-if-missing write, a top-level `var` of a built-in name in a classic script, a member write on a root) makes the program not intact. The result of a method call on a root or reached receiver is itself a reached value (`[].__proto__.valueOf()`, `globalThis.valueOf()`), except a listed static of a built-in and a global function called off the global object (`window.fetch(...)`, `this.toString()`, but not the inherited `valueOf`, which returns its receiver). A sloppy function's `this` may be the global object, so a member of it named like any built-in root or code runner (`this.Reflect`, `this.eval`) is reached too. A timer or scheduler named as a member of any receiver (`document.defaultView.setTimeout`, `o["setInterval"]`, a `const` key) is judged like the free timer: harmless only as a direct call whose first argument is a function; read as a value, destructured, or called through `call`/`apply`/`bind` or a tag it is not. A strict function whose value escapes to code the scan cannot see (an argument of any call, a value returned, thrown or yielded, an array element, a store on an object other than a local binding or under an `on...` key, a `call`/`apply`/`bind` of it, an export, or a top-level `var` or function of a classic script) may also be called with the global object as `this`, so its `this` is judged like a sloppy function's. A function only called directly, through `new`, or as a method of a local object that never escapes keeps a strict `this`; class methods and methods reached through an instance are not followed. A member named `eval`, `Function` or `execScript` on any receiver is a code runner (`document.defaultView.eval`, `e.currentTarget.Function`, a strict callback's `this.eval`), and so is a `vm` or loader runner under any receiver or destructuring key (`runInThisContext`, `runInNewContext`, `runInContext`, `compileFunction`, `module._compile`), also as a value or through `call`/`apply`/`bind`. A tagged template is a call: `` f`...` `` is judged like `f(...)`, so `` [].__proto__.valueOf`` `` is reached and `` setTimeout`...` `` runs a text. `__defineGetter__`, `__defineSetter__`, `__lookupGetter__` and `__lookupSetter__` count the same under any key spelling (`o["__defineGetter__"]`, a template literal, `?.[...]`, a literal concatenation or a `const`). Prototypes also count as reached when read under `__proto__`, `constructor`, `__lookupGetter__` or `__lookupSetter__` (as a member key, a destructuring key or a free name), through `getPrototypeOf`/`Reflect.get` on any root or reached owner, or under a computed key that is not a number, a string literal, a literal concatenation or a `const` initialised to one of these. Any `with` statement, and an `import()` or `import` of a `data:`, `blob:` or `javascript:` URL (or of a specifier that is not a literal) also count. The default lane assumes the program does not hand code text to a DOM API that evaluates it (`document.write`, a `javascript:` URL, `importScripts` of a `data:` URL, a script element's `text`, `textContent` or `src`, an event-handler attribute string or `setAttribute("on...")`). `--unsafe` assumes no built-in prototype is patched through a value the program reads; only a write whose target names the built-in (`Array.prototype.toString = ...`) is respected.
